\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Circuit Tree Manip}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.LMN.CircuitTreeManip
\section{Overview}

This module provides infrastructure for navigating and transforming the \texttt{Circuit}
tree type used in the LMN layer-reduction argument. It supplies De~Morgan dual
conversions between DNF and CNF, structural facts about circuit depth, and the
core ``absorb one level'' operation that folds the top level of a circuit into the
Layer~2 gates, lowering the circuit depth by at least one while keeping every gate
representable by a width-$l$ DNF and CNF.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[DNF to dual CNF]
\lean{LMN.dnfToDualCNF}
\label{LMN.dnfToDualCNF}
\leanok
\uses{CNF, DNF, Literal.flipNeg}
The De~Morgan dual of a DNF $\varphi$ on $n$ variables, obtained by negating every
literal of every term and reading the result as a CNF. Concretely
$\neg\big(\bigvee_i \bigwedge_j \ell_{ij}\big) = \bigwedge_i \bigvee_j \neg\ell_{ij}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Dual CNF preserves width]
\lean{LMN.dnfToDualCNF_width}
\label{LMN.dnfToDualCNF_width}
\leanok
\uses{CNF.width, DNF, DNF.width, LMN.dnfToDualCNF, Term.width}
\difficulty{2}
Let $\varphi$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables, that is, a list of terms, each term a
list of literals, and let its De Morgan dual CNF be obtained by negating every literal
of every term. Then the dual CNF has the same width as $\varphi$, where the width of a
formula is the maximum number of literals appearing in any of its terms (equal to $0$
when the formula is empty).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Dual CNF computes the negation of a DNF]
\lean{LMN.dnfToDualCNF_eval}
\label{LMN.dnfToDualCNF_eval}
\leanok
\uses{CNF.eval, CNF.evalClause, DNF, DNF.eval, LMN.dnfToDualCNF, Literal.flipNeg_eval, Term.eval}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\varphi$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables — a disjunction of terms, each term a
conjunction of literals — and let $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ be an assignment. Form its De~Morgan
dual CNF by negating every literal of every term of $\varphi$ and reading each resulting
term as a clause (a disjunction of literals), so that the whole is a conjunction of
clauses. Then this dual CNF evaluates on $x$ to the negation of the value of $\varphi$
on $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A circuit of positive depth is a gate]
\lean{LMN.Circuit.exists_node_of_depth_ge_one}
\label{LMN.Circuit.exists_node_of_depth_ge_one}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth}
\difficulty{2}
Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit whose depth is at least $1$. Then $c$ is not a literal: it
is an internal gate, so there exist a Boolean flag $\mathit{isAnd}$ and a list $cs$ of
child circuits for which $c$ is the node with gate type $\mathit{isAnd}$ applied to the
children $cs$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Children of a depth-one gate are literals]
\lean{LMN.Circuit.depth1_children_are_lits}
\label{LMN.Circuit.depth1_children_are_lits}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth}
\difficulty{4}
Let $C$ be the Boolean circuit consisting of a single gate (an AND gate or an OR gate,
according to a flag $\mathit{isAnd}$) applied to a list $cs$ of child circuits, so that
the depth of $C$ equals $1$ plus the maximum depth among the circuits in $cs$. If the
depth of $C$ is at most $1$, then every child circuit $c \in cs$ has depth $0$; that is,
each child is a literal.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Depth-zero circuits are literals]
\lean{LMN.Circuit.depth0_is_lit}
\label{LMN.Circuit.depth0_is_lit}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Lit}
\difficulty{2}
Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $m$ variables whose depth is $0$. Then $c$ is a leaf:
there exists a literal $l$ such that $c$ is the single-literal circuit built from $l$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Depth-one gates have only literal inputs]
\lean{LMN.Circuit.depth1_all_lits}
\label{LMN.Circuit.depth1_all_lits}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Lit, LMN.Circuit.depth0_is_lit, LMN.Circuit.depth1_children_are_lits}
\difficulty{1}
Fix a number of variables $m$, a gate type $isAnd \in \{\mathrm{true},
\mathrm{false}\}$, and a list $cs$ of Boolean circuits on $m$ variables, and form the
circuit $\mathrm{node}(isAnd, cs)$ whose root gate is applied to the children in $cs$.
If this circuit has depth at most $1$, then every child $c$ in $cs$ is a literal; that
is, there exists a literal $l$ with $c = \mathrm{lit}(l)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Child function under gate substitution]
\lean{LMN.childFunction}
\label{LMN.childFunction}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval}
The Boolean function on $\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}$ computed by a subcircuit
$c_{\mathrm{sub}}$ when each of its inputs $i$ is replaced by the gate function
$\mathrm{gates}\,i$, namely $x \mapsto c_{\mathrm{sub}}.\mathrm{eval}\,(\lambda i,\ \mathrm{gates}\,i\,x)$.
\end{definition}

\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.cleanDNF, LMN.cleanDNF_eval, LMN.cleanDNF_nodup, LMN.cleanDNF_var_inj, LMN.cleanDNF_width_le, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.dtDepth_le_implies_small_dnf_cnf, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{3}
Let $g_1,\dots,g_m$ be DNF formulas on $n$ Boolean variables, let $\rho$ be a
restriction of these variables, and let $l\in\bbn$. For each $i$, write $f_i$ for the
restriction of $g_i$ by $\rho$, that is, the Boolean function $x \mapsto
g_i(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ that evaluates $g_i$ with the coordinates fixed by $\rho$
set accordingly and the free coordinates supplied by $x$, and suppose that every $f_i$
has decision-tree depth at most $l$. Then for each $i$ there is a DNF formula
$\varphi_i$ of width at most $l$ that computes $f_i$, in which no term repeats a literal
and no two literals of the same term share a variable; and there is a CNF formula
$\psi_i$ of width at most $l$ that also computes $f_i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[DNF for an OR of literals over gate functions]
\lean{LMN.or_of_lit_children_dnf}
\label{LMN.or_of_lit_children_dnf}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, BoolCircuit.Lit, CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.compression_or_of_dnfs, cnfToDualDNF, cnfToDualDNF_eval, cnfToDualDNF_width}
\difficulty{5}
Fix natural numbers $m,n$ and a width bound $l$. Let $c_1,\dots,c_k$ be Boolean circuits
on $m$ variables, each of which is a single literal, and let $N$ be the OR node whose
children are exactly these circuits. Suppose that to each variable index $i \in
\mathrm{Fin}\,m$ there is associated a gate function $g_i$ taking a Boolean assignment
$x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \{0,1\}$ to a Boolean value, and that every $g_i$ is computed
both by some DNF formula on the $n$ inputs of width at most $l$ and by some CNF formula
on the $n$ inputs of width at most $l$. Then the composite function $x \mapsto
N\bigl((g_i(x))_{i}\bigr)$ — the disjunction of the literal children evaluated at the
gate values $g_i(x)$ — is itself computed by a DNF formula $\varphi$ on the $n$ inputs
of width at most $l$, in the sense that $\varphi(x)$ equals the value of $N$ on the
assignment $i \mapsto g_i(x)$ for every $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[AND of literal gates has a width-$l$ CNF]
\lean{LMN.and_of_lit_children_cnf}
\label{LMN.and_of_lit_children_cnf}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, BoolCircuit.Lit, CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.compression_and_of_cnfs, LMN.dnfToDualCNF, LMN.dnfToDualCNF_eval, LMN.dnfToDualCNF_width}
\difficulty{5}
Fix natural numbers $m$, $n$, and $l$, and let $g_0, \dots, g_{m-1}$ be Boolean
functions of an input $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \{0,1\}$, one for each index $i \in
\mathrm{Fin}\,m$, such that each $g_i$ is computed both by some DNF of width at most $l$
and by some CNF of width at most $l$. Let the circuits $c \in cs$ each be a single
literal over the variables $0, \dots, m-1$, and let $C$ be the AND gate whose children
are exactly these literals, evaluated on an input $x$ by substituting the value $g_i(x)$
for the $i$-th variable. Then the Boolean function computed in this way — the
conjunction of the literal values $g_i(x)$ or their negations — is itself represented by
a CNF $\psi$ of width at most $l$, in the sense that $\psi$ evaluates to $C$'s value on
every input $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Absorbing a depth-one top gate into the second layer]
\lean{LMN.absorbOneLevel_depth1}
\label{LMN.absorbOneLevel_depth1}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.Circuit.depth1_all_lits, LMN.Circuit.exists_node_of_depth_ge_one, LMN.Layer2Data, LMN.and_of_lit_children_cnf, LMN.cleanDNF, LMN.cleanDNF_eval, LMN.cleanDNF_nodup, LMN.cleanDNF_var_inj, LMN.cleanDNF_width_le, LMN.or_of_lit_children_dnf, cnfToDualDNF, cnfToDualDNF_eval, cnfToDualDNF_width}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\mathrm{data}$ be layer-2 data over $n$ Boolean variables: a family of gates, each
computing a DNF formula, sharing a common positive width bound. Let $c_{\mathrm{top}}$
be a Boolean circuit whose input variables are indexed by these gates, and fix an
integer $l \ge 1$. Suppose that $c_{\mathrm{top}}$ has depth exactly $1$ (a single AND
or OR gate applied to literals in the gate outputs), and that each gate computes a
function that is representable both by a DNF of width at most $l$ — one in which, within
every term, distinct literals carry distinct variables and no literal is repeated — and
by a CNF of width at most $l$. Then there exist layer-2 data $\mathrm{data}'$ of width
at most $l$ and a circuit $c_{\mathrm{top}}'$ of depth $0$ over the gates of
$\mathrm{data}'$ such that, for every Boolean assignment $x$ to the $n$ variables, the
value of $c_{\mathrm{top}}$ evaluated on the outputs of the gates of $\mathrm{data}$
equals the value of $c_{\mathrm{top}}'$ evaluated on the outputs of the gates of
$\mathrm{data}'$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Signed width-$l$ DNF for a depth-$\le 1$ gate over subcircuits]
\lean{LMN.child_depth_le1_has_signed_dnf}
\label{LMN.child_depth_le1_has_signed_dnf}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, BoolCircuit.Lit, CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.Circuit.depth1_all_lits, LMN.Circuit.exists_node_of_depth_ge_one, LMN.and_of_lit_children_cnf, LMN.cleanDNF, LMN.cleanDNF_eval, LMN.cleanDNF_nodup, LMN.cleanDNF_var_inj, LMN.cleanDNF_width_le, LMN.or_of_lit_children_dnf, cnfToDualDNF, cnfToDualDNF_eval, cnfToDualDNF_width}
\difficulty{5}
Fix natural numbers $m,n,l$. Let $c_j$ be a Boolean circuit whose $m$ inputs are indexed
by $\mathrm{Fin}\,m$ and whose depth is at most $1$, and let $\mathrm{gates}$ assign to
each index $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,m$ a Boolean function $\mathrm{gates}_i \colon
(\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2) \to \bbf_2$. Suppose that every $\mathrm{gates}_i$ is
computed by some DNF over $n$ variables of width at most $l$, and also by some CNF over
$n$ variables of width at most $l$. Then there exist a DNF $\varphi$ over $n$ variables
of width at most $l$ and a sign bit $s \in \mathrm{Bool}$ such that, for every
assignment $x \colon \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2$, the value $\varphi$ takes at $x$ when
$s = \mathrm{true}$, and its negation when $s = \mathrm{false}$, equals the value of
$c_j$ under the assignment $i \mapsto \mathrm{gates}_i(x)$; moreover, each term of
$\varphi$ contains no repeated literal, and no two of its literals share a variable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Signed DNFs for depth-one circuits over gates]
\lean{LMN.list_child_signed_dnfs}
\label{LMN.list_child_signed_dnfs}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.child_depth_le1_has_signed_dnf}
\difficulty{3}
Let $g_1,\dots,g_m \colon \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be Boolean functions, and suppose that
each $g_i$ is computed both by a DNF formula of width at most $l$ and by a CNF formula
of width at most $l$. Let $C_1,\dots,C_k$ be Boolean circuits on $m$ inputs, each of
depth at most $1$. Then for every $j \in \{1,\dots,k\}$ there exist a DNF formula
$\varphi_j$ on the $n$ variables and a sign $\varepsilon_j \in
\{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}$ such that $\varphi_j$ has width at most $l$, each term
of $\varphi_j$ contains every variable at most once (so no term repeats a literal or
carries a variable in both polarities), and, for every assignment $x \in \{0,1\}^n$, the
value $\varphi_j(x)$ when $\varepsilon_j = \mathrm{true}$ and $\lnot\varphi_j(x)$ when
$\varepsilon_j = \mathrm{false}$ equals $C_j\bigl(g_1(x),\dots,g_m(x)\bigr)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A depth-one circuit for a single gate over literals]
\lean{LMN.build_literal_circuit}
\label{LMN.build_literal_circuit}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval}
\difficulty{3}
Fix an arity $k$, a gate type given by a flag that selects AND when true and OR when
false, and a family of polarities $\sigma : \mathrm{Fin}\,k \to \mathbb{F}_2$. For each
variable index $j \in \mathrm{Fin}\,k$, let $\ell_j$ be the literal on variable $j$ with
polarity $\sigma(j)$, and let $G$ be the single gate of the chosen type applied to the
list $\ell_0, \ell_1, \dots, \ell_{k-1}$. Then there is a Boolean circuit $c'$ of depth
at most $1$ that computes the same Boolean function as $G$: for every assignment $g :
\mathrm{Fin}\,k \to \mathbb{F}_2$, the value of $c'$ at $g$ equals the value of $G$ at
$g$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Depth reduction for depth-one composed circuits]
\lean{LMN.exists_circuit_depth_reduction_depth1}
\label{LMN.exists_circuit_depth_reduction_depth1}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.child_depth_le1_has_signed_dnf}
\difficulty{2}
Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $m$ inputs of depth exactly $1$, and let $g_1,\dots,g_m
\colon (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2) \to \bbf_2$ be Boolean functions on $n$ variables,
each of which is computed by some DNF formula of width at most $l$ and also by some CNF
formula of width at most $l$. Then the composed function $x \mapsto
c\big(g_1(x),\dots,g_m(x)\big)$ — obtained by feeding $g_i(x)$ into the $i$-th input of
$c$ — is, up to an overall sign, computed by a single DNF formula of width at most $l$
each of whose terms has no repeated literal and mentions every variable at most once (in
particular no term contains both a variable and its negation). Precisely, there exist
such a DNF formula $\varphi$ and a sign bit $s$ so that, for every $x$, $\varphi(x) =
c\big(g_1(x),\dots,g_m(x)\big)$ when $s$ is positive and $\lnot\varphi(x) =
c\big(g_1(x),\dots,g_m(x)\big)$ when $s$ is negative.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Depth reduction for depth-2 circuits over narrow gates]
\lean{LMN.exists_circuit_depth_reduction_depth2}
\proofsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{
  pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004,
  pdf-fc447f326910-p013-b002
}
\proofsource{switching-lemma}{pdf-b5e074215b9e-p004-b002}
\label{LMN.exists_circuit_depth_reduction_depth2}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.Circuit.exists_node_of_depth_ge_one, LMN.build_literal_circuit, LMN.list_child_signed_dnfs}
\difficulty{6}
Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit of depth exactly $2$ on $m$ inputs, and let $g_1,\dots,g_m
\colon \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be Boolean functions such that each $g_i$ is computed both
by a DNF formula of width at most $l$ and by a CNF formula of width at most $l$, where
the width of a DNF or CNF formula is the maximum number of literals occurring in any
single one of its terms or clauses. Then there exist a number $m'$, DNF formulas
$D_1,\dots,D_{m'}$ on $n$ variables, and a Boolean circuit $c'$ of depth at most $1$ on
$m'$ inputs, such that each $D_j$ has width at most $l$, every term of every $D_j$
contains each variable at most once (equivalently, its literals are pairwise distinct
and no two of them share a variable), and for every assignment $x \in \{0,1\}^n$,
\[ c\bigl(g_1(x),\dots,g_m(x)\bigr) = c'\bigl(D_1(x),\dots,D_{m'}(x)\bigr). \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Merging child reductions into a shared gate family]
\lean{LMN.reduce_children}
\label{LMN.reduce_children}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width}
\difficulty{3}
Fix a number of variables $n$ and let assignments $x$ range over $\{0,1\}^n$. Let
$C_1,\dots,C_r$ be Boolean circuits, each on the same set of $m$ inputs, and let
$\gamma_1,\dots,\gamma_m$ be functions assigning to every assignment $x$ a bit, so that
feeding input $i$ the value $\gamma_i(x)$ turns each $C_j$ into a Boolean function of
$x$. Fix a width bound $l$ and, for each $j$, a depth bound $b_j$. Assume every child
admits a DNF reduction: for each $j$ there are a Boolean circuit $c_j$ of depth at most
$b_j$ on some number $m_j$ of inputs, together with DNF formulas
$g_{j,1},\dots,g_{j,m_j}$ over $x_1,\dots,x_n$, each of width at most $l$ and each of
whose terms has its literals on pairwise distinct variables, such that
\[ C_j\big(i \mapsto \gamma_i(x)\big) = c_j\big(k \mapsto g_{j,k}(x)\big) \qquad \text{for every } x. \]
Then these per-child families can be amalgamated into a single one: there exist a family
of DNF formulas $h_1,\dots,h_M$ over $x_1,\dots,x_n$, each of width at most $l$ and each
with all its terms' literals on pairwise distinct variables, together with circuits
$C'_1,\dots,C'_r$ on these $M$ shared inputs, such that $\mathrm{depth}(C'_j) \le b_j$
and
\[ C'_j\big(k \mapsto h_k(x)\big) = C_j\big(i \mapsto \gamma_i(x)\big) \qquad \text{for every } j \text{ and every } x. \]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gate value is preserved under child-wise equality]
\lean{LMN.node_eval_eq_of_finRange_map}
\label{LMN.node_eval_eq_of_finRange_map}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval}
\difficulty{5}
Fix a Boolean flag $\mathit{isAnd}$ and a finite list $c_1,\dots,c_k$ of Boolean
circuits on $m$ variables, and let $d_1,\dots,d_k$ be Boolean circuits on $M$ variables,
one for each position of the list. Given assignments $g : \mathrm{Fin}\,m \to \bbf_2$
and $g' : \mathrm{Fin}\,M \to \bbf_2$ such that every re-indexed child agrees with the
corresponding original child, i.e. $d_j$ evaluated at $g'$ equals $c_j$ evaluated at $g$
for each position $j$, the gate node with flag $\mathit{isAnd}$ over $c_1,\dots,c_k$
evaluated at $g$ equals the gate node with the same flag $\mathit{isAnd}$ over
$d_1,\dots,d_k$ evaluated at $g'$. Here the node is the conjunction of its children's
values when $\mathit{isAnd} = \mathrm{true}$ and their disjunction when $\mathit{isAnd}
= \mathrm{false}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Depth reduction for circuits with CNF and DNF gates]
\lean{LMN.exists_circuit_depth_reduction}
\statementsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{
  pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004,
  pdf-fc447f326910-p013-b002
}
\statementsource{switching-lemma}{
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p004-b002,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p004-b003
}
\label{LMN.exists_circuit_depth_reduction}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, BoolCircuit.Lit.eval, CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.Circuit.exists_node_of_depth_ge_one, LMN.child_depth_le1_has_signed_dnf, LMN.exists_circuit_depth_reduction_depth1, LMN.exists_circuit_depth_reduction_depth2, LMN.node_eval_eq_of_finRange_map, LMN.reduce_children}
\difficulty{6}
Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit on $m$ inputs whose depth is at least $1$, and suppose each
input coordinate $i$ is fed by a Boolean function $g_i \colon \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$, so
that $c$ computes the map $x \mapsto c\bigl(g_1(x),\dots,g_m(x)\bigr)$. Fix a width
bound $l \ge 1$, and assume that every $g_i$ is computed both by a DNF formula of width
at most $l$, each of whose terms contains at most one literal per variable, and by a CNF
formula of width at most $l$. Then there exist a number of inputs $m'$, Boolean
functions $g'_1,\dots,g'_{m'}$ each presented as a DNF formula of width at most $l$ with
the same restriction that no term contains two literals in the same variable, and a
circuit $c'$ of depth at most $\mathrm{depth}(c) - 1$, such that
$c\bigl(g_1(x),\dots,g_m(x)\bigr) = c'\bigl(g'_1(x),\dots,g'_{m'}(x)\bigr)$ for every
assignment $x$.
\end{lemma}

\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.Layer2Data, LMN.exists_circuit_depth_reduction}
\difficulty{2}
Let $D$ be layer-2 data over $n$ variables: a family of DNF gates $g_0,\dots,g_{m-1}$
together with a common positive width bound. Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit whose $m$
inputs are indexed by these gates and whose depth is at least $2$, and let $l\ge 1$.
Suppose that for each index $i$ the gate $g_i$ admits a DNF formula of width at most $l$
that computes the same Boolean function as $g_i$ and in which, within every term,
distinct literals use distinct variables and no literal is repeated, as well as a CNF
formula of width at most $l$ computing that same Boolean function. Then there exist
layer-2 data $D'$ over $n$ variables of width at most $l$, with gate family
$h_0,\dots,h_{k-1}$, and a Boolean circuit $C'$ whose $k$ inputs are indexed by these
gates and whose depth is at most $\mathrm{depth}(C)-1$, such that for every assignment
$x\colon\mathrm{Fin}\,n\to\{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}$ the value of $C$ on the
input vector $\bigl(g_i(x)\bigr)_i$ equals the value of $C'$ on the input vector
$\bigl(h_j(x)\bigr)_j$.
\end{lemma}

\uses{BoolCircuit.Circuit, BoolCircuit.Circuit.depth, BoolCircuit.Circuit.eval, CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.Layer2Data, LMN.absorbOneLevel_depth1, LMN.absorbOneLevel_general}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n, l \in \bbn$ with $l \ge 1$, and let $\mathcal{D}$ be a layer-2 datum on $n$
variables whose gates $g_0, \dots, g_{m-1}$ are DNF formulas. Let $C$ be a Boolean
circuit on $m$ inputs — one per gate — with $\mathrm{depth}(C) \ge 1$, and consider the
composite Boolean function $x \mapsto C\bigl(g_0(x), \dots, g_{m-1}(x)\bigr)$. Suppose
that each gate $g_i$ admits both a DNF representation $\varphi_i$ of width at most $l$
computing the same function as $g_i$ — one in which, within every term, any two literals
sharing a variable coincide and no literal is repeated — and a CNF representation of
width at most $l$ computing that same function. Then there exist a layer-2 datum
$\mathcal{D}'$ on $n$ variables of width at most $l$, with gates $g'_0, \dots,
g'_{m'-1}$, and a Boolean circuit $C'$ on $m'$ inputs with $\mathrm{depth}(C') \le
\mathrm{depth}(C) - 1$, such that for every assignment $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2$,
\[
  C\bigl(g_0(x), \dots, g_{m-1}(x)\bigr) = C'\bigl(g'_0(x), \dots, g'_{m'-1}(x)\bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}
